import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 126

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/126](https://www.erdosproblems.com/126)
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos126

def IsMaximalAddFactorsCard (f : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop := ∀ n,
    IsGreatest
      { m | ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), A.card = n →
        m ≤ (∏ ⟨a, b⟩ ∈ A.offDiag, (a + b)).primeFactors.card}
      (f n)

/--
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ has $|A| = n$ then
$\prod_{a\neq b\in A}(a + b)$ has at least $f(n)$ distinct prime factors.
Is it true that $\frac{f(n)}{\log n} \to\infty$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_126 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ), IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f →
    Tendsto (fun n => f n / Real.log n) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Turán proved [ErTu34] in their first joint paper that
$$
  \log n \ll f(n) \ll \frac{n}{\log n}
$$

[ErTu34] Erdős, Paul and Turan, Paul, _On a Problem in the Elementary Theory of Numbers_. Amer. Math. Monthly (1934), 608-611.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_126.variants.IsBigO
    (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hf : IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f) :
    ((fun (n : ℕ) => Real.log n) =O[atTop] fun (n : ℕ) => (f n : ℝ)) ∧
      (fun (n : ℕ) => (f n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun (n : ℕ) => n / Real.log n := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős says that $f(n) = o(\frac{n}{\log n})$ has never been proved.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_126.variants.isLittleO
    (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hf : IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f) :
    (fun (n : ℕ) => (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) => n / Real.log n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos126

status_issues.source_status: The current problem page records an affirmative, Lean-verified solution. It credits GPT-6 Astra with the stronger bound f(n) ≫ n^(1/2). The page was last edited 3 September 2026.
status_issues.evidence: https://erdosproblems.com/126 says “PROVED (LEAN)” and “This has been solved in the affirmative and the proof verified in Lean.” Its LaTeX source, https://erdosproblems.com/latex/126, states: “This was proved by GPT-6 Astra ... which in fact proved that $f(n)\gg n^{1/2}$.”
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research solved` and replace `answer(sorry)` with `answer(True)`, leaving the mathematical right-hand side unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The primary paper uses sets of distinct positive integers, whereas `Finset ℕ` permits zero. The extremal functions can therefore differ at small inputs, but all three claims in this file are unchanged.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let f₀ be the minimum prime count over nonnegative n-element sets and f₊ the corresponding minimum over positive sets. For every n, f₀(n) ≤ f₊(n) ≤ f₀(n+1): positive sets are admissible nonnegative sets, and any (n+1)-element nonnegative set contains an n-element positive subset. Products are positive, so taking a subset cannot increase their distinct-prime count. These inequalities and the stability of log n and n/log n under shifting n by one imply equivalence of the main divergence claim, both big-O bounds, and the little-o claim. All three equivalences, together with the sandwich inequalities and existence/uniqueness of the extremal function, were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the problem's sorry theorems.
